picks.what: The town with the Epiphany Monastery and the castle walls, woodcut
picks.why: earliest view of the town, labeled “Град Могилев”, from a book printed in 1702 or 1703; this copy shows the town larger than #3

picks.what: The Great Synagogue on Vilenskaya Street, magazine illustration from a photograph
picks.why: only usable 19th-century picture of the town: a street with its best-known synagogue; caption trimmed

gaps: P0–P1: nothing; P3: only maps, a town plan and documents; P5: only 1941 vertical aerial photos (map-like, one marking a destroyed bridge) and a portrait of Nicholas II; P6: only road junctions and factory smokestacks
notes: #13 is the weakest pick (a single building in a street, a halftone from the magazine Niva); drop it if a blank plate is preferred. #9 is Gomel, not Mogilev, and #11 is a 1912 painting of an 1812 battle near the town.
